text:
IncidentBot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-2234 — router_p95_latency_us-east1 > 800ms (service: runtime-router). Auto-escalation in 5m if unacked. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/router-latency
Maya Chen: acked — i'm taking this. looking at grafana now, p95 jumped ~900ms across a small subset of hosts.
Luis Ortega: thx maya. any customer-facing errors in SLO dashboards or support queue?
Maya Chen: no support tickets yet, no visible 5xx spike. sounds like latency-only. plotting traces now.
Kai Patel: quick heads-up — router-4 shows KC (kv) cache warmup activity, lots of cold misses and CPU on that pod spiking to 93%. might be a warmup flurry after a deployment?
Maya Chen: good catch. i'm going to cordon and restart router-4 to see if it falls back to steady state. rolling one at a time.
Maya Chen: command: ```kubectl cordon router-4 && kubectl drain router-4 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data && kubectl delete pod router-4 -n prod```
IncidentBot: note: this thread is an automated page — keep updates here for auditing.
PagerDuty: Alert PD-2234 acknowledged by Maya Chen (on-call).
Kai Patel: after restart, router-4 memory falls and p95 trending down. other routers showing transient KV miss spikes but within expected noise.
Maya Chen: p95 back to ~180ms on restarted node, cluster p95 dropping to 210ms overall. marking as mitigated.
IncidentBot: PD-2234 auto-resolved by monitoring: latency metric back under threshold for 3 consecutive minutes.
Luis Ortega: nice. no customer impact per support and no 5xx increase. we'll create a short follow-up: add synthetic canary for KV warmup and adjust alert suppression for bursts.
Kai Patel: agree — create playbook note and consider staggered warmup or small cache priming during deploys.
Maya Chen: filing a quick follow-up issue: https://redwood.internal/ops/ISSUE-4821 (will add runbook tweak + canary). closing thread. :white_check_mark:
